There is a LS from SA5 on the Handover terminology in [1]. In which, SA5 categorizes handover to 5 type. SA5 notes that the following kinds of handovers need to be explicitly defined. Note that items 2 and 3 are already explicitly defined: Currently, SA5 interprets "Legacy HO" as the most basic form of HO where a single HO target is configured and where HO preparation happens right before HO execution while the UE disconnects from source before it re-connects to the target. SA5 asks RAN2 and RAN3 to develop terminology for separating the different kinds of handover. In the meantime, RAN2 agreed two CRs in [1] and [2] to remove the ambiguous term ‘legacy’ or ‘normal’ handovers from TS 36.300 and TS 38.300. The reply LS from RAN2 is in [3]. [3] (ran3_tdoc_chunks R3-211998, sim=0.4829)
Based on the discussion above, we have the following observations and proposals. Observation 1: In releases before Rel-16 in NR and LTE, The term of ‘Handover’ implies that the HO will execute right after the UE receives the HO command message from network. Observation 2: ‘Immediate handover’ is defined in RAN3 stage 3 specification to distinguish Conditional handover. Proposal 1: RAN3 to confirm that the term ‘handover’ remains its original meaning in Rel-15. R el-16 CHO and DAPS handover are just some “optimization” of the handover. Proposal 2: it is proposed to reply SA5 in the reply LS that: The term ’handover’ still remains its original meaning in Rel-15. Defining a term including all handover types for the purpose of KPIs is up to SA5. The reply LS is provided in [4]. R2-2103338, CR

[6] (ran3_tdoc_chunks R3-212306, sim=0.4713)
In [1] RAN3 received an LS asking “RAN3 to develop terminology for separating "legacy" handover from handovers in general”. This paper discusses the LS and provides a way forward. The LS in [1] points at the existence of different types of handovers and categorises these as follows: "Ordinary" or "Legacy" Handover. Conditional Handover, CHO. See TS 38.00 clause 3.2. Dual Active Protocol Stack Handover, DAPS Handover. See TS 38.300 clause 3.2. Possible future forms of handover, yet to be specified. Note that in the future, CHO might be considered a "legacy" handover type. Handovers in general, including items 1 to 4. With regards to what is referred above as “"Ordinary" or "Legacy" Handover”, it is our understanding that this can be referred to as what described in section 9.2.3.1 of TS38.3
